title: Head of Growth Marketing, PLG
description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation - building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

Location: San Francisco Bay Area - Hybrid

Reports to: Chief Marketing Officer

CodeRabbit helps engineering teams review code with higher signal, stronger context, and less drag on the pull-request workflow. As AI-generated code increases, the bottleneck moves downstream - teams still need to catch risk, understand intent, and merge with confidence.

We're hiring a Head of Growth Marketing, PLG to own the self-serve motion that's already showing real traction. Twenty-five percent of our revenue is already self-serve - developers and engineers are finding CodeRabbit, adopting it, and paying for it on their own. This role is about scaling what's working.

You'll own how individual developers discover, activate, and convert - managing all paid channels and leading a team of media planners and creatives to maximize both volume and efficiency across the self-serve funnel.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the full self-serve / PLG growth motion - from acquisition strategy to channel execution to funnel optimization.

- Manage all paid acquisition channels: search, display, social, sponsorships, and emerging channels - with clear targets for volume, efficiency, and CAC.

- Build and optimize direct-to-developer and direct-to-consumer acquisition programs that drive signups, activation, and conversion.

- Lead and develop a team of media planners and creatives, setting a high bar for quality and performance.

- Define the metrics that matter - CAC, LTV, ROAS, activation rates - and use them to make better investment decisions.

- Partner with Product and Engineering on growth experiments, onboarding improvements, and conversion opportunities.

- Identify and test new acquisition channels before they become obvious.

- Translate channel performance into clear business outcomes for senior leadership.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- 8+ years in growth marketing or paid acquisition leadership, including ownership of a company-level self-serve or PLG growth number.

- Deep experience running direct-to-consumer and/or direct-to-developer acquisition programs at scale.

- Proven track record managing all paid channels - search, display, social, sponsorships - with measurable results.

- Experience leading a team of media planners and creatives.

- Strong analytical mindset - you optimize with data, not instinct, and you can prove it.

- Ability to balance volume and efficiency simultaneously - you know when to scale and when to cut.

- Experience in a high-growth startup or scale-up where you've had to build while running.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience marketing technical products to developers or engineering teams.

- Familiarity with developer tools, AI infrastructure, or the modern software development lifecycle.

- Experience taking a product from strong organic pull to a mature multi-channel acquisition engine.

What success looks like

- More developers and engineering teams are finding CodeRabbit through repeatable, scalable acquisition channels.

- Paid programs are running efficiently with clear attribution and improving unit economics over time.

- The self-serve funnel converts faster, with a clearer path from first touch to activated user.

title: Air Refueling Operator
description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service - spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack - from the lab to the field - we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Air Mobility Group (AIRMOB) is responsible for developing and delivering Metrea’s aerial refueling (AAR) capabilities, ensuring the readiness and operational effectiveness of the tanker fleet. AIRMOB oversees fleet management, maintenance, and airworthiness, working to sustain and enhance refueling operations. It manages the integration of new processes and technologies, ensuring that tanker aircraft remain mission-ready through effective logistics, maintenance oversight, and regulatory compliance. title: PhD Researcher: AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content Generation
description:
About the position

You are expected to contribute to the development of internationally visible, foundational research in AI-driven semantic structure extraction, automated reasoning-flow modeling, and adaptive content generation. The research focuses on methods for analyzing and representing deep semantic and pedagogical structures in scientific and educational materials; high-fidelity extraction of conceptual and reasoning blocks; inference-time rationale generation; and adaptive, learner-aware sequencing of content. This includes work on semantic parsing, structured NLP, graph-based neural models, metacognitive prompting, ontology alignment across disciplines, and human-in-the-loop optimization.

In this context, interdisciplinary research is strongly encouraged-particularly collaborations spanning computer science, computational linguistics, cognitive science, and the learning sciences. You will contribute to developing datasets, baseline models, personalized learning engines, reasoning-graph representations, cross-domain mapping algorithms, and RLHF-style feedback loops that improve system interpretability and instructional quality. The successful candidate will also contribute to high-quality publications, release research prototypes, and support demonstrator systems that deliver structured semantic extraction, rationale-aware content generation, and cross-domain transfer of reasoning structures.

Additionally, the successful candidate is expected to support teaching activities in areas such as Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, AI in Education, Knowledge Representation, and Python-based analytical seminars at the BSc, MSc, and PhD levels. Responsibilities include assisting in course delivery, advising students, supervising Bachelor/Master theses, and engaging in methodological innovation for online, hybrid, and in-person learning environments. The university provides strong support

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. title: Tax Software QA & Support Analyst
description:
This role is fully remote, open to candidates based anywhere in the United States outside New York, with a preference for the Pacific or Mountain time zones. Based in New York? Apply to the New York posting of this role instead.
A Different Kind Of Job Description
At Filed , we believe in radical transparency. Everything is open: company finances, team salaries, stock options, anonymous team feedback. That extends to how we talk about this job. So instead of a list of perks, we'll start with what's genuinely hard about it, then tell you why it might be the best move you'll make.
What's hard about this job
Bugs don't arrive with instructions. A customer tells you "it didn't work." Your job is to work out exactly what they did, with which return, in which tax software, and make it happen again on your own screen. If you can't reproduce it, engineering can't fix it.
Your ticket is the fix's starting point. Engineers will build from what you write. Vague steps mean days of back and forth while a firm waits. You'll need to be precise every time.
The pace is fast. Our customers are tax firms in their busiest weeks. When something breaks, they need an answer today, and a workaround while the real fix is built.
It isn't fixed until you've checked. You'll retest every fix before telling a customer it's resolved, and you'll recheck after releases that nothing else broke.
Why it might be the best career move you'll make
You'll sit between customers and engineering. Few roles see both sides this clearly. You'll learn how real firms use tax software, and how software actually gets built.
Your work ships. A bug you reproduce on Monday becomes a fix every firm on Filed benefits from. A workaround you find saves a firm hours the same day.
You'll grow as fast as we do. Filed is adding millions of dollars of revenue every quarter, and the support and QA function is still small. People who start here move into QA, product and engineering-adjacent roles.
We've raised $17.2 million to date, led by Northzone, and we work with tax firms across the country, from regional practices to some of the biggest names in the profession.
What You'll Own

• Reproducing customer-reported issues step by step, inside Filed and the tax software firms already use

• Writing clear, complete Linear tickets with exact steps, expected versus actual results, screenshots and sample data, so engineers can act straight away

• Answering customer tickets quickly and clearly in our support inbox

• Troubleshooting technical issues and finding workarounds that keep firms moving

• Verifying fixes before they go back to the customer, and regression testing after releases

• Spotting patterns across tickets and flagging them before they spread

Your Hard Skillset

• Hands-on QA or software testing experience: you've reproduced bugs and written them up for an engineering team

• Customer support experience in a ticketing system such as Pylon, Zendesk, Intercom or Freshdesk

• A tax background, either at a tax or accounting firm, at a tax software company, or preparing returns yourself. You don't need to be a preparer, but you should know your way around a return.

• Familiarity with at least one major tax platform, such as CCH Axcess, UltraTax, Lacerte, ProConnect, Drake or GoSystem

• Bonus if you've used Linear or Jira, browser developer tools or screen recording to capture issues

Your Soft Skillset

• Methodical: you change one thing at a time until you find what breaks

• Clear writing: your tickets and replies leave no room for confusion

• Curious: you want to know why something broke, not just that it did

• Calm and patient with customers who are under deadline pressure

• You take ownership and follow a problem through to the fix

Who This Suits

• People who enjoy hunting down a problem more than answering the same question twice

• Support professionals who want to move into QA and product

• Tax professionals who want to move into tech without leaving their expertise

We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.
We’re looking for an experienced Data Analyst who has built evaluation systems for complex technology products and is excited to take end-to-end ownership of quality in search built for AI agents.
This role combines hands-on engineering, analytical judgment, and mathematical rigor, with the scope and influence to shape both technical decisions and product direction. We move at a startup pace, with plenty of open questions and difficult problems to solve.

In this position, you will:

• Own the quality measurement and improvement cycle end-to-end: identify user needs, define success, build evaluations, diagnose failures, and work with engineers and product managers to improve outcomes..
• Design, build, and evolve evaluation systems, including datasets, benchmarks, metrics, and automated pipelines that support development and launch decisions..

• Investigate quality regressions and metric anomalies, uncover root causes, and identify the improvements with the greatest potential impact..

We expect you to have:

• A track record of owning ambiguous problems from initial framing through implementation, diagnosis, and measurable product improvement..
• Strong Python skills and an engineering mindset: you can turn analytical ideas into reliable, maintainable pipelines and tools..
• A solid foundation in mathematical statistics and practical experience with experimental design, sampling, uncertainty, and measurement bias..
• Strong analytical judgment: you understand what a metric captures, what it misses, and whether an observed improvement matters to users..
• The ability to reason across user needs, product behavior, and technical systems, and to translate that understanding into actionable evaluations..
• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence technical and product decisions..
• The independence to make progress in a fast-moving environment where requirements, methods, and definitions of success are still evolving.

• Competitive compensation

• Career growth and learning opportunities

• Flexibility and ownership

• Collaborative and innovative culture

• Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

• International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

title: Community Support Engineer
description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the governance and control layer for agentic software development, helping engineering teams trust the code they ship. AI can generate code faster than people can review and understand it. Teams still need to know whether each change solves the right problem, fits their architecture, and is safe to ship.

We provide independent validation grounded in codebase context and team standards, giving people the evidence they need to judge what should ship. Across Review, Triage, Explain, and Secure, our platform challenges changes before merge, prioritizes pull requests by value, impact, and risk, explains what changed and why it matters, and monitors the codebase for security vulnerabilities after merge.

CodeRabbit serves nearly 20,000 customers and supports approximately 300,000 open-source repositories, performing over 2 million code reviews each week. Our $143M Series C, raised at a $1.5B valuation, supports further product development and international expansion.

Locations: San Fransisco, CA or Boston, MA (Boston preferred)- Hybrid

ROLE OVERVIEW

This role will be the first point of contact for technical questions across CodeRabbit’s public communities, including Discord, X, Reddit, and GitHub Discussions. The responsibility is to troubleshoot code review issues, resolve integration problems, answer technical questions, and follow through until the issue is resolved. When an issue requires Engineering or Product involvement, the expectation is to create a ticket with enough technical detail and context for the team to take action without unnecessary back-and-forth. Unlike traditional support, these interactions happen in public, where other users can see the responses. Providing clear, accurate, and timely answers is important not only for helping the customer but also for building trust in CodeRabbit Support and making solutions available to others facing similar issues.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Collaborate with marketing and Devrel to engage CodeRabbit community spaces-Discord, X, GitHub discussions, Reddit- for support-relevant posts and questions from developers.

2. Troubleshoot customer code review scenarios, integration failures, and API issues end-to-end. Reproduce issues, debug code, and deliver working solutions.

3. Synthesize patterns from community questions into searchable, reusable resources: how-to guides, debugging walkthroughs, config examples, and known gotchas.

4. Escalate thoughtfully to engineering and product teams when bugs, missing features, or product improvements are identified. Open tickets with full reproduction steps and context.

5. Operate asynchronously across APAC, EMEA, and AMER timezones. Prioritize response speed and clarity in public community spaces.

6. Partner with support engineers on complex issues. Own community resolution; facilitate escalations to enterprise support when needed.

7. Build trust and foster community health: recognize quality peer answers, encourage knowledge-sharing, and maintain welcoming, technical tone.

8. Report community insights and trends to leadership: recurring issues, feature requests, product feedback, and gaps in documentation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Great candidates often have these qualifications:

1. At least 4 years of experience leading support operations initiatives, program management, or operational improvements in a technical/SaaS environment

2. Proven track record of designing and launching operational programs or initiatives that measurably improved support metrics and team productivity

3. Strong analytical mindset with fluency in operational data-able to define metrics, interpret dashboards, and translate insights into programs and process improvements

4. Customer Obsession: a passion to deliver a high-quality customer experience

5. Systems thinking and operational strategy: ability to design scalable frameworks, establish standards, and evolve how support operates at scale
